## Task 1: Session check-in

### Three interesting or exciting things

1. I learned that a regular `ggplot()` graph can be made interactive with `ggplotly()`, allowing viewers to explore individual observations by hovering over points.
2. I learned that the information shown in a tooltip can be customized by creating a text label that combines multiple variables from the dataset.
3. I found it interesting that a Quarto dashboard can bring different types of information together, including an interactive map, value boxes, and a data visualization, in one webpage.

### Three muddy or unclear things

1. I am still learning how to control the exact appearance and placement of information in interactive plot tooltips.
2. The dashboard layout options and the way rows and columns determine the size of each element are still a little unclear.
3. I would like more practice understanding the publishing process and how changes to the project files update the live website.

## Task 2: Interactive plot

The plot below compares penguin bill depth and bill length. Color and point shape distinguish the three species. Hover over a point to see the species, sex, island, bill depth, and bill length.

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| warning: false
#| message: false

library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)
library(palmerpenguins)
library(glue)

penguins <- palmerpenguins::penguins |>
  drop_na(sex) |>
  rename(
    bill_dep = bill_depth_mm,
    bill_len = bill_length_mm
  )
```

### Recreate plot

```{r}
#| label: interactive-penguin-plot
#| warning: false

penguins_labeled <- penguins |>
  mutate(
    label = glue(
      "{species} ({sex} on {island} Island)<br>",
      "Bill depth: {bill_dep} mm<br>",
      "Bill length: {bill_len} mm"
    )
  )

p <- ggplot(
  penguins_labeled,
  aes(
    x = bill_dep,
    y = bill_len,
    color = species,
    shape = species,
    text = label
  )
) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("darkorange", "purple", "cyan4")) +
  labs(
    x = "Bill depth (mm)",
    y = "Bill length (mm)",
    color = "Species",
    shape = "Species"
  ) +
  theme_light()

# Convert the static ggplot into an interactive plotly graphic.
ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text")
```
